But people who have nothing will lose even the little they have.

es.L: Y dijo a los que estaban presentes: “{{plural_you:Quítenle|Quitadle}} la mina y {{plural_you:dénsela|dádsela}} al que tiene las diez minas”. \v 25 Y le dijeron: “Señor, ¡tiene diez minas!”. \v 26 “{{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que a todo el que tiene, se le dará [más]; pero al que no tiene, aun lo que tiene se le quitará.
es.B: Entonces dijo a los que estaban allí: “{{plural_you:Quítenle|Quitadle}} la mina y {{plural_you:dénsela|dádsela}} al que tiene diez”. \v 25 “Señor —le dijeron—, ¡si ya tiene diez minas!”. \v 26 “{{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que a todo el que tiene se le dará más. Pero al que no tiene nada se le quitará hasta lo que tiene.
es.R: Luego el rey dijo a los hombres que estaban a su lado: “{{plural_you:Quítenle|Quitadle}} la mina a este siervo. {{plural_you:Dénsela|Dádsela}} al siervo que tiene diez minas”. \v 25 Ellos le dijeron: “Pero, señor, ¡él ya tiene diez minas!”. \v 26 El rey respondió: “{{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que a quien tiene algo se le dará más. Pero a quien no tiene nada se le quitará hasta lo poco que tiene.

fr.L: Et il a dit à ceux qui se tenaient là : “Enlevez-lui la mine et donnez[-la] à celui qui a les dix mines.” \v 25 Et ils lui ont dit : “Maître, il a dix mines !” \v 26 “Je vous dis qu’à quiconque a, [davantage] sera donné ; mais à celui qui n’a pas, même ce qu’il a sera enlevé.
fr.B: Puis il a dit à ceux qui étaient là : “Prenez-lui la mine et donnez-la à celui qui en a dix.” \v 25 “Maître, lui ont-ils dit, il a déjà dix mines !” \v 26 “Je vous le dis : à celui qui a, on donnera davantage. Mais celui qui n’a rien perdra même ce qu’il a.
fr.R: Ensuite, le roi a dit aux hommes qui se tenaient près de lui : “Enlevez la mine à ce serviteur. Donnez-la au serviteur qui a dix mines.” \v 25 Ils lui ont dit : “Mais maître, il a déjà dix mines !” \v 26 Le roi a répondu : “Je vous le dis : les gens qui ont quelque chose recevront davantage. Mais les gens qui n’ont rien perdront même le peu qu’ils ont.

sw.L: Naye akawaambia wale waliosimama karibu, 'Mnyang'anyeni ile mina, mkampe yule mwenye mina kumi.' \v 25 Nao wakamwambia, 'Bwana, ana mina kumi!' \v 26 'Nawaambia kwamba kila aliye na kitu atapewa [zaidi], lakini asiye na kitu, hata kile alicho nacho kitaondolewa kwake.
sw.B: Kisha akawaambia wale waliokuwa wamesimama pale, 'Mnyang'anyeni mina hiyo, mkampe yule mwenye mina kumi.' \v 25 Wakamwambia, 'Bwana, tayari ana mina kumi!' \v 26 'Nawaambia, kila aliye na kitu ataongezewa. Lakini asiye na kitu atanyang'anywa hata kile alicho nacho.
sw.R: Kisha mfalme akawaambia watu waliosimama karibu naye, 'Mnyang'anyeni mtumishi huyu mina hiyo. Mpeni mtumishi mwenye mina kumi.' \v 25 Wakamwambia, 'Lakini bwana, tayari ana mina kumi!' \v 26 Mfalme akajibu, 'Nawaambia, watu walio na kitu wataongezewa zaidi. Lakini watu wasio na kitu watanyang'anywa hata kile kidogo walicho nacho.

decisions.choice: 19:25, the bystanders' protest: included, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: 19:25 left out, as in a few manuscripts
decisions.reason: Almost all manuscripts have the verse. A few, among them Codex Bezae, leave it out, perhaps because it interrupts the king's words. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: they said ...; I tell you: the bystanders interrupt, and the king answers them
alternatives: 19:26 is Jesus speaking to his hearers, outside the story
decisions.reason: "I tell you" could be Jesus stepping out of the parable, as in 18:8, 14. But 19:27 goes on with the king's words ("these enemies of mine"), so 19:26 is best read as the king's reply to the protest.

decisions.choice: to everyone who has, more will be given: those who use what God gives receive more; those who do not, lose it
decisions.reason: Jesus said the same about hearing his word (8:18). What a person "has" is what he has made good use of. The slave who did nothing loses even the mina.

decisions.choice: those standing by: attendants of the king
decisions.reason: Those standing by are the king's servants at his court, who carry out his orders.

decisions.choice: will be given; will be taken away: by the king, in the story
decisions.reason: The passives describe what the king does; in the lesson, what God does.

decisions.choice: Master
decisions.reason: As in 19:16. In the story the word is the title a slave gives the man who owns him; "Lord" would make him sound like God.

decisions.choice: mina (every level)
decisions.reason: The amount is explained once, in Readable at 19:13 and in the meaning decision there. Repeating a modern sum each time the servants speak would make the dialogue hard to follow, so every level keeps the unit's own name. "Pound", the older rendering, now suggests British money.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they have|he has}} (L, B); the little they have (R)
decisions.reason: The saying is about anyone; Greek speaks of such a person with a masculine form. Readable uses plural words for people, which need no setting.

decisions.choice: The king answered
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker of 19:26 (m2).

decisions.choice: the king's words in 19:26 open a quotation that continues to the end of 19:27
decisions.reason: 19:27 goes on with what the king says.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on the commands and on "{{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo"
decisions.reason: The king speaks to the attendants standing by (meaning decision m4), so every "you" is plural and takes the ustedes / vosotros setting. English has no such choice.

decisions.choice: no gender span
decisions.reason: The English needs "they have|he has" for the one who has nothing. Spanish "lo que tiene" has no pronoun that differs between an inclusive and a traditional wording, so no setting applies.

decisions.choice: celui qui n’a pas (rien) ... ce qu’il a (L, B), with no gender span
alternatives: a gender setting on the pronoun, as the English "they have / he has"
decisions.reason: As the style guide says, "celui qui" already means anyone in French, and the "il" that refers back to it is ordinary generic French, so French needs no setting where the English needs one. Readable uses plural words for people, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: no gender span
decisions.reason: The English needs "they have|he has" for the one who has nothing. Swahili "alicho nacho" and "kwake" already mean he or she, so no setting applies.

source.text: πλὴν τοὺς ἐχθρούς μου τούτους τοὺς μὴ θελήσαντάς με βασιλεῦσαι ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ἀγάγετε ὧδε καὶ κατασφάξατε αὐτοὺς ἔμπροσθέν μου.

records.literal_gloss: But the enemies of me these, the [ones] not having wanted me to reign over them, bring here and slaughter them before me.

en.L: But these enemies of mine, who did not want me to reign over them, bring here and slay them before me.'"
en.B: As for these enemies of mine who did not want me as their king, bring them here and execute them in my presence.'"
en.R: And bring here those enemies of mine who did not want me to be their king. Kill them right here in front of me!'"

es.L: Pero a estos enemigos míos, los que no quisieron que yo reinara sobre ellos, {{plural_you:tráiganlos|traedlos}} acá y {{plural_you:degüéllenlos|degolladlos}} delante de mí”».
es.B: Y en cuanto a estos enemigos míos que no me querían por rey, {{plural_you:tráiganlos|traedlos}} aquí y {{plural_you:ejecútenlos|ejecutadlos}} en mi presencia”».
es.R: Y {{plural_you:traigan|traed}} aquí a esos enemigos míos que no querían que yo fuera su rey. ¡{{plural_you:Mátenlos|Matadlos}} aquí mismo, delante de mí!”».

fr.L: Mais ces ennemis, les miens, qui n’ont pas voulu que je règne sur eux, amenez-les ici et égorgez-les devant moi.” »
fr.B: Quant à mes ennemis, ceux qui ne voulaient pas de moi pour roi, amenez-les ici et exécutez-les en ma présence.” »
fr.R: Et ces ennemis qui ne voulaient pas que je sois leur roi, amenez-les ici. Tuez-les ici même, devant moi !” »

sw.L: Lakini adui zangu hawa, wale wasiotaka niwatawale, waleteni hapa mkawachinje mbele yangu.'"
sw.B: Na kuhusu adui zangu hawa ambao hawakutaka niwe mfalme wao, waleteni hapa, mkawaue mbele yangu.'"
sw.R: Tena waleteni hapa wale adui zangu ambao hawakutaka niwe mfalme wao. Waueni hapa hapa mbele yangu!'"

decisions.choice: these enemies: in the story, the citizens who rejected the king; Jesus warns of judgment on those who reject him
decisions.reason: The words belong to the king in the story, and they finish what began in 19:14. Kings of the time often put rebels to death when they took power. Jesus is about to enter Jerusalem, where he will weep over the city's coming judgment (19:41-44).

decisions.choice: slaughter: kill, put to death
decisions.reason: The verb is a strong one, used of slaughtering animals and of killing in battle.

decisions.choice: but: now turning to another matter
decisions.reason: The word marks a change of subject: from the slaves to the enemies.

decisions.choice: the parable ends here, closing the king's words and Jesus' speech
decisions.reason: Jesus' speech began at 19:12.

source.text: Καὶ εἰπὼν ταῦτα ἐπορεύετο ἔμπροσθεν ἀναβαίνων εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.

records.literal_gloss: And having said these [things] he was going ahead going up to Jerusalem.

en.L: And having said these things, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
en.B: After saying this, Jesus went on ahead of them, going up to Jerusalem.
en.R: When Jesus had finished telling this story, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went on ahead of the others on the road up to Jerusalem.

es.L: Y habiendo dicho estas cosas, iba delante, subiendo a Jerusalén.
es.B: Después de decir esto, Jesús siguió adelante, delante de ellos, subiendo hacia Jerusalén.
es.R: Cuando Jesús terminó de contar esta historia, siguió caminando delante de los demás por el camino que sube a Jerusalén.

fr.L: Et, après avoir dit ces choses, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} marchait devant, montant à Jérusalem.
fr.B: Après avoir dit cela, Jésus partit devant eux pour monter à Jérusalem.
fr.R: Quand Jésus a fini de raconter cette histoire, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a continué la route devant les autres, en montant vers Jérusalem.

sw.L: Na akiisha kusema hayo, alienda mbele, akipanda kwenda Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Baada ya kusema hayo, Yesu aliendelea mbele yao, akipanda kwenda Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Yesu alipomaliza kuwaambia mfano huo, alitangulia mbele ya wengine katika njia inayopanda kwenda Yerusalemu.

decisions.choice: going up to Jerusalem: climbing from Jericho to the city
decisions.reason: Jerusalem stands in the hills, and the road from Jericho climbs steeply. People spoke of going up to Jerusalem whatever direction they came from (2:42; 18:31).

decisions.choice: went on ahead: leading the way to the city where he would suffer
decisions.reason: Since 9:51 Jesus has set his face to go to Jerusalem. He leads his followers there, knowing what will happen (18:31-33).

decisions.choice: of them (B); of the others (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek "ahead" means ahead of those with him.

source.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἤγγισεν εἰς Βηθφαγὴ καὶ Βηθανίαν πρὸς τὸ ὄρος τὸ καλούμενον Ἐλαιῶν, ἀπέστειλεν δύο τῶν μαθητῶν λέγων· Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν κατέναντι κώμην, ἐν ᾗ εἰσπορευόμενοι εὑρήσετε πῶλον δεδεμένον, ἐφ’ ὃν οὐδεὶς πώποτε ἀνθρώπων ἐκάθισεν, καὶ λύσαντες αὐτὸν ἀγάγετε.

records.literal_gloss: And it came about as he drew near to Bethphage and Bethany toward the mount the [one] being called of Olives, he sent two of the disciples \v 30 saying, Go into the opposite village, in which entering you will find a colt having been tied, on which no one ever of men has sat, and having untied it bring [it].

en.L: And it happened, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} drew near to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount that is called [the Mount] of Olives, [that] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent two of the disciples, \v 30 saying, "Go into the village opposite, where on entering you will find a colt tied, on which no one has ever yet sat. Untie it and bring [it].
en.B: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came near Bethphage and Bethany, by the hill called the Mount of Olives, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent off two of the disciples. \v 30 "Go to the village ahead of you," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them. "As you go into it, you will find a young donkey tied there, one that nobody has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it here.
en.R: Jesus came near the villages of Bethphage and Bethany, at the hill called the Mount of Olives. There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent two of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers ahead. \v 30 He said to them, "Go into the village in front of you. As soon as you go in, you will find a young donkey tied up. No one has ever ridden it. Untie it and bring it to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando se acercó a Betfagé y Betania, junto al monte llamado de los Olivos, envió a dos de los discípulos, \v 30 diciendo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a la aldea de enfrente, en la cual, al entrar, {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}} un pollino atado, sobre el cual ningún hombre se ha sentado jamás; {{plural_you:desátenlo|desatadlo}} y {{plural_you:tráiganlo|traedlo}}.
es.B: Cuando se acercaba a Betfagé y a Betania, junto al cerro llamado monte de los Olivos, envió a dos de los discípulos. \v 30 «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a la aldea que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} delante —les dijo—. Al entrar en ella, {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}} atado un pollino que nadie ha montado nunca. {{plural_you:Desátenlo|Desatadlo}} y {{plural_you:tráiganlo|traedlo}} aquí.
es.R: Jesús se acercó a los pueblos de Betfagé y Betania, junto al cerro llamado monte de los Olivos. Allí envió por delante a dos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. \v 30 Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} al pueblo que está ahí delante. En cuanto {{plural_you:entren|entréis}}, {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}} un burrito atado. Nadie lo ha montado nunca. {{plural_you:Desátenlo|Desatadlo}} y {{plural_you:tráiganmelo|traédmelo}}.

fr.L: Et il arriva, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} approchait de Bethphagé et de Béthanie, vers le mont appelé [mont] des Oliviers, [qu’]{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} envoya deux des disciples, \v 30 disant : « Allez au village qui est en face ; en y entrant, vous trouverez un poulain attaché, sur lequel personne n’est encore jamais monté ; détachez-le et amenez[-le].
fr.B: Comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} approchait de Bethphagé et de Béthanie, près de la colline qu’on appelle le mont des Oliviers, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} envoya deux des disciples. \v 30 « Allez au village qui est devant vous, leur dit-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}. En y entrant, vous trouverez un ânon attaché, que personne n’a encore jamais monté. Détachez-le et amenez-le ici.
fr.R: Jésus est arrivé près des villages de Bethphagé et de Béthanie, près de la colline qu’on appelle le mont des Oliviers. Là, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a envoyé deux de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples en avant. \v 30 Il leur a dit : « Allez dans le village qui est devant vous. Dès que vous y entrerez, vous trouverez un jeune âne attaché. Personne ne l’a encore jamais monté. Détachez-le et amenez-le-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: Ikawa alipokaribia Bethfage na Bethania, karibu na mlima uitwao [Mlima] wa Mizeituni, aliwatuma wawili wa wanafunzi, \v 30 akisema, "Nendeni katika kijiji kilicho mkabala, ambamo mtakapoingia mtamkuta mwana-punda amefungwa, ambaye juu yake hajapata kuketi mtu yeyote kamwe; mfungueni, mmlete.
sw.B: Alipokaribia Bethfage na Bethania, karibu na kilima kiitwacho Mlima wa Mizeituni, aliwatuma wanafunzi wawili. \v 30 Akawaambia, "Nendeni katika kijiji kilicho mbele yenu. Mtakapoingia humo, mtamkuta mwana-punda amefungwa, ambaye hajawahi kupandwa na mtu yeyote. Mfungueni, mmlete hapa.
sw.R: Yesu alikaribia vijiji vya Bethfage na Bethania, karibu na kilima kiitwacho Mlima wa Mizeituni. Huko aliwatuma wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wawili watangulie. \v 30 Akawaambia, "Nendeni katika kijiji kilicho mbele yenu. Mara mtakapoingia, mtamkuta punda mchanga amefungwa. Hakuna mtu aliyewahi kumpanda. Mfungueni, mmlete {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}.

decisions.choice: Bethphage and Bethany, the Mount of Olives: villages on the hill east of Jerusalem, on the road from Jericho
decisions.reason: The Mount of Olives faces Jerusalem across the Kidron valley. Bethany lay about two miles from the city (John 11:18), and Bethphage was nearer. Zechariah 14:4 speaks of the LORD standing on the Mount of Olives on the day he comes.

decisions.choice: colt: a young animal, here a young donkey
decisions.reason: The word means the young of an animal. Mark 11:2 and John 12:14-15 show it was a donkey, as in Zechariah 9:9, where Zion's king comes humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt.

decisions.choice: on which no one has ever sat: an animal not yet used, fit for a sacred purpose
decisions.reason: Animals set apart for God were ones that had never been put to work (Numbers 19:2; Deuteronomy 21:3; 1 Samuel 6:7).

decisions.choice: the colt: Jesus comes as the king of Zechariah 9:9
decisions.reason: Jesus had walked all the way from Galilee. Riding into the city on a colt acts out the prophecy of the humble king (Zechariah 9:9), which Matthew 21:5 and John 12:15 quote.

decisions.choice: young donkey
decisions.reason: Today a colt is usually a young horse. Balanced and Readable say what animal it was (m2); Literal keeps "colt".

decisions.choice: Jesus' words open here and continue to the end of 19:31
decisions.reason: His instructions go on in 19:31.

decisions.choice: to me
decisions.reason: Readable says where to bring it.

decisions.choice: discípulos at every level
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "followers"; the shared term sheet keeps "discípulos" at every level in Spanish, a word Spanish readers know, so the Gospels read alike.

decisions.choice: pollino (L, B); burrito (R)
decisions.reason: A colt here is a young donkey (meaning decision m2). "Pollino" is the word for it, as in Matthew 21; Readable uses the everyday "burrito".

decisions.choice: un poulain (L); un ânon (B); un jeune âne (R)
alternatives: un poulain at Literal and Balanced, as in Mark 11
decisions.reason: The word names the young of an animal, here a young donkey (m2). Literal keeps the general word, as the English keeps "colt". The English Balanced says "young donkey" here, and French has a plain word for it, "ânon"; Readable says "jeune âne", as in Mark 11. This holds for 19:30-35.

decisions.choice: disciples at every level, Readable included
decisions.reason: English Readable says "followers"; as in Mark, French keeps "les disciples" at every level, where the word is familiar and plain. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: wanafunzi at every level
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "followers"; the shared term sheet keeps "wanafunzi" at every level in Swahili, as in John, so the Gospels read alike.

decisions.choice: mwana-punda (L, B); punda mchanga (R)
decisions.reason: A colt here is a young donkey (meaning decision m2). "Mwana-punda" is the word used in Matthew 21; Readable says plainly "punda mchanga", a young donkey.

source.text: καὶ ἐάν τις ὑμᾶς ἐρωτᾷ· Διὰ τί λύετε;

records.literal_gloss: And if anyone you asks, Why are you untying?

en.L: And if anyone asks you, 'Why are you untying [it]?'
en.B: If anyone asks you, 'Why are you untying it?'
en.R: If anyone asks you, 'Why are you untying the donkey?'

es.L: Y si alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} pregunta: “¿Por qué [lo] {{plural_you:desatan|desatáis}}?”,
es.B: Si alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} pregunta: “¿Por qué lo {{plural_you:desatan|desatáis}}?”,
es.R: Si alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} pregunta: “¿Por qué {{plural_you:desatan|desatáis}} al burrito?”,

fr.L: Et si quelqu’un vous demande : “Pourquoi [le] détachez-vous ?”
fr.B: Si quelqu’un vous demande : “Pourquoi le détachez-vous ?”
fr.R: Si quelqu’un vous demande : “Pourquoi détachez-vous cet âne ?”

sw.L: Na mtu akiwauliza, 'Mbona mnamfungua?'
sw.B: Mtu yeyote akiwauliza, 'Kwa nini mnamfungua?'
sw.R: Mtu yeyote akiwauliza, 'Kwa nini mnamfungua punda huyo?'

decisions.choice: if anyone asks: the first half of one instruction, finished in the next sentence
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT ends the sentence at the question mark of the quoted question; the answer follows in the next sentence.

decisions.choice: no closing double quotation mark; Jesus' words continue
decisions.reason: The instruction is finished in 19:31b.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:les|os}}, {{plural_you:desatan|desatáis}} and the other words to the two disciples
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" (the default) and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. The same through the chapter.

source.text: οὕτως ἐρεῖτε ὅτι Ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ χρείαν ἔχει.

records.literal_gloss: thus you will say, that The Lord of it need has.

en.L: you shall say this: 'The Lord has need of it.'"
en.B: tell them, 'The Lord needs it.'"
en.R: tell them, 'The Lord needs it.'"

es.L: así {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}}: “El Señor tiene necesidad de él”».
es.B: {{plural_you:díganle|decidle}}: “El Señor lo necesita”».
es.R: {{plural_you:díganle|decidle}}: “El Señor lo necesita”».

fr.L: vous direz ainsi : “Le Seigneur en a besoin.” »
fr.B: répondez-lui : “Le Seigneur en a besoin.” »
fr.R: dites-lui : “Le Seigneur en a besoin.” »

sw.L: mtasema hivi, 'Bwana ana haja naye.'"
sw.B: mwambieni, 'Bwana anamhitaji.'"
sw.R: mwambieni, 'Bwana anamhitaji.'"

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus
decisions.reason: The disciples speak of Jesus by the title Luke uses of him (19:8). Some take it to mean God, or the colt's owner if he was with Jesus, but the owners are in the village (19:33). The words are spoken with authority, as the king claims what he needs.

decisions.choice: of it: the Lord needs the colt
alternatives: the Lord of it, its owner
decisions.reason: The pronoun goes with "need", not with "Lord".

source.text: ἀπελθόντες δὲ οἱ ἀπεσταλμένοι εὗρον καθὼς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Having gone away then the [ones] having been sent found just as he had said to them.

en.L: And those who were sent went away and found [it] just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had told them.
en.B: Those who had been sent went off and found things just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had told them.
en.R: So the two disciples went and found everything just as Jesus had told them.

es.L: Y habiéndose ido los enviados, [lo] encontraron tal como les había dicho.
es.B: Los enviados fueron y encontraron todo tal como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les había dicho.
es.R: Los dos discípulos fueron y encontraron todo tal como Jesús les había dicho.

fr.L: Et ceux qui avaient été envoyés s’en allèrent et trouvèrent [tout] comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le leur avait dit.
fr.B: Les envoyés partirent et trouvèrent tout comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le leur avait dit.
fr.R: Les deux disciples sont partis. Ils ont trouvé tout comme Jésus le leur avait dit.

sw.L: Basi wale waliotumwa wakaenda, wakakuta kama alivyowaambia.
sw.B: Wale waliotumwa walikwenda, wakakuta mambo yote kama alivyowaambia.
sw.R: Basi wale wanafunzi wawili walikwenda, wakakuta kila kitu kama Yesu alivyowaambia.

decisions.choice: just as he had told them: Jesus' word proves true
decisions.reason: Luke shows Jesus knowing what will happen (22:10-13). Whether he had arranged it beforehand is not said; the point is that his words are fulfilled.

decisions.choice: the two disciples
decisions.reason: Readable says who they were (19:29).

source.text: λυόντων δὲ αὐτῶν τὸν πῶλον εἶπαν οἱ κύριοι αὐτοῦ πρὸς αὐτούς· Τί λύετε τὸν πῶλον;

records.literal_gloss: Untying then of them the colt said the owners of it to them, Why are you untying the colt?

en.L: And as they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, "Why are you untying the colt?"
en.B: As they were untying the young donkey, its owners asked them, "Why are you untying the donkey?"
en.R: While they were untying the young donkey, its owners asked them, "Why are you untying our donkey?"

es.L: Y mientras ellos desataban el pollino, sus dueños les dijeron: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:desatan|desatáis}} el pollino?».
es.B: Mientras desataban el pollino, sus dueños les preguntaron: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:desatan|desatáis}} el pollino?».
es.R: Mientras desataban el burrito, sus dueños les preguntaron: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:desatan|desatáis}} nuestro burrito?».

fr.L: Et comme ils détachaient le poulain, ses propriétaires leur dirent : « Pourquoi détachez-vous le poulain ? »
fr.B: Pendant qu’ils détachaient l’ânon, ses propriétaires leur demandèrent : « Pourquoi détachez-vous cet ânon ? »
fr.R: Pendant qu’ils détachaient le jeune âne, ses propriétaires leur ont demandé : « Pourquoi détachez-vous notre âne ? »

sw.L: Na walipokuwa wakimfungua mwana-punda, wenyewe wakawaambia, "Mbona mnamfungua mwana-punda?"
sw.B: Walipokuwa wakimfungua mwana-punda, wenye mwana-punda waliwauliza, "Kwa nini mnamfungua mwana-punda?"
sw.R: Walipokuwa wakimfungua punda mchanga, wenye punda waliwauliza, "Kwa nini mnamfungua punda wetu?"

decisions.choice: owners: the people the colt belonged to
decisions.reason: The same word that means "lord" here means the owners of property. Luke sets them beside "the Lord" who needs it (19:34).

decisions.choice: owners
decisions.reason: The sense here is ownership (m1).

decisions.choice: young donkey; donkey
decisions.reason: As in 19:30.

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν ὅτι Ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ χρείαν ἔχει.

records.literal_gloss: They then said that The Lord of it need has.

en.L: And they said, "The Lord has need of it."
en.B: They answered, "The Lord needs it."
en.R: They answered, "The Lord needs it."

es.L: Y ellos dijeron: «El Señor tiene necesidad de él».
es.B: Ellos respondieron: «El Señor lo necesita».
es.R: Ellos respondieron: «El Señor lo necesita».

fr.L: Et ils dirent : « Le Seigneur en a besoin. »
fr.B: Ils répondirent : « Le Seigneur en a besoin. »
fr.R: Ils ont répondu : « Le Seigneur en a besoin. »

sw.L: Nao wakasema, "Bwana ana haja naye."
sw.B: Wakajibu, "Bwana anamhitaji."
sw.R: Wakajibu, "Bwana anamhitaji."

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus, as in 19:31
decisions.reason: The disciples give the answer Jesus told them to give, and the owners let them go. Luke contrasts the owners with the Lord who has a greater claim.

source.text: καὶ ἤγαγον αὐτὸν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ ἐπιρίψαντες αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ἐπὶ τὸν πῶλον ἐπεβίβασαν τὸν Ἰησοῦν·

records.literal_gloss: And they brought it to the Jesus, and having thrown of them the cloaks on the colt they set on [it] the Jesus;

en.L: And they brought it to Jesus, and throwing their cloaks on the colt, they set Jesus on [it].
en.B: They brought the donkey to Jesus, threw their cloaks over it, and helped Jesus get on.
en.R: They brought the young donkey to Jesus. They put their coats on the donkey's back, and they helped Jesus get up on it.

es.L: Y lo llevaron a Jesús, y echando sus mantos sobre el pollino, montaron [en él] a Jesús.
es.B: Llevaron el pollino a Jesús, le echaron encima sus mantos y ayudaron a Jesús a montar.
es.R: Le llevaron el burrito a Jesús. Pusieron sus capas sobre el lomo del burrito y ayudaron a Jesús a subirse.

fr.L: Et ils l’amenèrent à Jésus, et, ayant jeté leurs manteaux sur le poulain, ils firent monter Jésus [dessus].
fr.B: Ils amenèrent l’ânon à Jésus, jetèrent leurs manteaux dessus et aidèrent Jésus à y monter.
fr.R: Ils ont amené le jeune âne à Jésus. Ils ont mis leurs manteaux sur son dos, et ils ont aidé Jésus à monter dessus.

sw.L: Wakamleta kwa Yesu, na wakiisha kutupa mavazi yao juu ya mwana-punda, wakampandisha Yesu [juu yake].
sw.B: Walimleta mwana-punda kwa Yesu, wakatandika mavazi yao ya nje juu yake, wakamsaidia Yesu kupanda.
sw.R: Walimleta punda mchanga kwa Yesu. Wakaweka makoti yao mgongoni mwa punda, wakamsaidia Yesu apande juu yake.

decisions.choice: cloaks: outer garments, used here as a saddle
decisions.reason: The cloak was the outer robe, worn over the tunic and used as a blanket at night (6:29). The disciples use theirs to make a seat for Jesus.

decisions.choice: they set Jesus on it: as Solomon was set on David's mule to be made king
decisions.reason: When Solomon was to be made king, David had him ride on the king's own mule into the city (1 Kings 1:33-40). Jesus is honored as a king by his followers.

decisions.choice: helped Jesus get on
decisions.reason: The verb means to put someone on a mount. Balanced and Readable say it in plain words.

decisions.choice: coats
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word for the outer garment.

decisions.choice: mantos (L, B); capas (R)
decisions.reason: The outer garment, laid on the colt as a saddle (meaning decision m1). The term used through the Gospels; Readable's "capas" matches the English Readable's "coats" without suggesting a modern overcoat.

decisions.choice: mavazi (L); mavazi ya nje (B); makoti (R)
decisions.reason: The outer garment, laid on the colt as a saddle (meaning decision m1). The term used through the Gospels; Readable's "makoti" matches the English Readable's "coats".

source.text: πορευομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ὑπεστρώννυον τὰ ἱμάτια ἑαυτῶν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Going then of him they were spreading the cloaks of themselves on the road.

en.L: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went along, they were spreading their cloaks on the road.
en.B: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rode along, people spread their cloaks on the road.
en.R: As Jesus rode along, people spread their coats on the road in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} avanzaba, extendían sus mantos en el camino.
es.B: Mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} avanzaba montado, la gente tendía sus mantos en el camino.
es.R: Mientras Jesús avanzaba montado, la gente extendía sus capas en el camino delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Et tandis qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avançait, ils étendaient leurs manteaux sur le chemin.
fr.B: À mesure qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avançait, les gens étendaient leurs manteaux sur la route.
fr.R: Pendant que Jésus avançait sur l’âne, les gens ont étendu leurs manteaux sur la route devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Naye alipokuwa akienda, walikuwa wakitandika mavazi yao njiani.
sw.B: Alipokuwa akiendelea na safari, watu walitandika mavazi yao ya nje barabarani.
sw.R: Yesu alipokuwa akiendelea kupanda punda, watu walitandika makoti yao barabarani mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

decisions.choice: spreading their cloaks on the road: honoring a new king
decisions.reason: When Jehu was anointed king, the commanders spread their cloaks under him and proclaimed him king (2 Kings 9:13). The people greet Jesus as king.

decisions.choice: they were spreading: people kept spreading them as he went
decisions.reason: The imperfect describes something done again and again along the way. Luke does not mention branches, as Matthew 21:8 and Mark 11:8 do.

decisions.choice: in front of him
decisions.reason: Readable says where they spread them.

source.text: ἐγγίζοντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἤδη πρὸς τῇ καταβάσει τοῦ Ὄρους τῶν Ἐλαιῶν ἤρξαντο ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος τῶν μαθητῶν χαίροντες αἰνεῖν τὸν θεὸν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ περὶ πασῶν ὧν εἶδον δυνάμεων, λέγοντες· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος βασιλεὺς ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου· ἐν οὐρανῷ εἰρήνη καὶ δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις.

records.literal_gloss: Drawing near then of him already at the descent of the Mount of the Olives they began all the multitude of the disciples rejoicing to praise the God with a voice loud for all which they had seen mighty works, \v 38 saying, Blessed the coming king in [the] name of [the] Lord; in heaven peace and glory in highest [places].

en.L: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was now drawing near, at the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began, rejoicing, to praise God with a loud voice for all the works of power that they had seen, \v 38 saying, "Blessed [is] the King who comes in [the] name of [the] Lord! In heaven peace, and glory in [the] highest!"
en.B: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came close to the city, where the road goes down the Mount of Olives, the whole crowd of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples began to praise God joyfully and loudly for all the mighty deeds they had seen. \v 38 They shouted, "Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!"
en.R: Jesus came near the place where the road goes down from the Mount of Olives to Jerusalem. There the whole crowd of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers began to praise God. They were full of joy, and they shouted loudly to thank God for all the miracles they had seen. \v 38 They said, "Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! There is peace in heaven, and glory to God in the highest heaven!"

es.L: Y acercándose {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ya a la bajada del monte de los Olivos, toda la multitud de los discípulos, gozosos, comenzó a alabar a Dios a gran voz por todas las obras poderosas que habían visto, \v 38 diciendo: «¡Bendito el Rey que viene en [el] nombre del Señor! ¡En [el] cielo paz, y gloria en [las] alturas!».
es.B: Cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ya estaba cerca de la ciudad, donde el camino baja del monte de los Olivos, toda la multitud de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos comenzó a alabar a Dios con alegría y a grandes voces por todas las obras poderosas que habían visto. \v 38 Gritaban: «¡Bendito el Rey que viene en el nombre del Señor! ¡Paz en el cielo, y gloria en las alturas!».
es.R: Jesús llegó cerca del lugar donde el camino baja del monte de los Olivos hacia Jerusalén. Allí toda la multitud de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos comenzó a alabar a Dios. Estaban llenos de alegría y gritaban fuerte para darle gracias a Dios por todos los milagros que habían visto. \v 38 Decían: «¡Bendito el Rey que viene en el nombre del Señor! ¡Hay paz en el cielo, y gloria a Dios en lo más alto del cielo!».

fr.L: Et comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} approchait déjà de la descente du mont des Oliviers, toute la multitude des disciples, se réjouissant, se mit à louer Dieu d’une voix forte pour tous les actes de puissance qu’ils avaient vus, \v 38 disant : « Béni [soit] le Roi qui vient au nom du Seigneur ! Dans le ciel paix, et gloire dans les lieux très hauts ! »
fr.B: Comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} arrivait près de la ville, là où la route descend du mont des Oliviers, toute la foule de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, pleine de joie, se mit à louer Dieu à grands cris pour tous les actes puissants qu’ils avaient vus. \v 38 Ils criaient : « Béni soit le Roi qui vient au nom du Seigneur ! Paix dans le ciel, et gloire au plus haut des cieux ! »
fr.R: Jésus est arrivé près de l’endroit où la route descend du mont des Oliviers vers Jérusalem. Là, toute la foule de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples s’est mise à louer Dieu. Les gens étaient pleins de joie, et ils criaient fort pour remercier Dieu de tous les miracles qu’ils avaient vus. \v 38 Ils disaient : « Béni soit le Roi qui vient au nom du Seigneur ! Il y a la paix dans le ciel, et gloire à Dieu au plus haut des cieux ! »

sw.L: Na alipokuwa akikaribia, tayari kwenye mteremko wa Mlima wa Mizeituni, umati wote wa wanafunzi ulianza kumsifu Mungu kwa furaha kwa sauti kubwa kwa ajili ya matendo yote ya nguvu waliyokuwa wameyaona, \v 38 wakisema, "[Amebarikiwa] Mfalme anayekuja kwa jina la Bwana! Mbinguni amani, na utukufu katika [mbingu] zilizo juu kabisa!"
sw.B: Alipokaribia mji, mahali ambapo njia inateremka kutoka Mlima wa Mizeituni, umati wote wa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ulianza kumsifu Mungu kwa furaha na kwa sauti kubwa, kwa sababu ya matendo yote ya nguvu waliyoyaona. \v 38 Walipaza sauti, "Amebarikiwa Mfalme anayekuja kwa jina la Bwana! Amani mbinguni, na utukufu huko juu kabisa!"
sw.R: Yesu alifika karibu na mahali ambapo njia inateremka kutoka Mlima wa Mizeituni kwenda Yerusalemu. Hapo umati wote wa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ulianza kumsifu Mungu. Walijaa furaha, wakapaza sauti kubwa kumshukuru Mungu kwa miujiza yote waliyokuwa wameiona. \v 38 Walisema, "Amebarikiwa Mfalme anayekuja kwa jina la Bwana! Kuna amani mbinguni, na utukufu kwa Mungu juu kabisa mbinguni!"

decisions.choice: Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord: Psalm 118:26, with "the King" added; in the Hebrew, "Lord" is the divine name
decisions.reason: Psalm 118 was sung by pilgrims at the great festivals. Its verse 26 blesses the one who comes in the name of the LORD; the disciples add "the King". Jesus himself quoted the verse in 13:35. To come in the Lord's name is to come sent by God and with his authority.

decisions.choice: blessed: praised, spoken well of before God
decisions.reason: This is not the word of the beatitudes (6:20-22), which says someone is fortunate, but the word used for praising God (1:68) and for those on whom God's blessing rests (1:42).

decisions.choice: peace in heaven, and glory in the highest: peace with God is settled in heaven, and God is praised there
alternatives: a wish: let there be peace in heaven
decisions.reason: The words echo the angels' song at Jesus' birth: glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace (2:14). Here the disciples speak of peace in heaven. God has made peace through the king who comes, and heaven gives him the glory. Luke does not have the cry "Hosanna" found in the other Gospels.

decisions.choice: works of power: miracles
decisions.reason: As in 10:13, the word means acts that show power.

decisions.choice: the descent of the Mount of Olives: where the road from Bethany crests the hill and Jerusalem comes into view
decisions.reason: From the top of the Mount of Olives the road goes down toward the city, which lies across the valley in full view (19:41).

decisions.choice: the whole multitude of the disciples: the large company of his followers, not only the twelve
decisions.reason: Luke speaks of a great company of disciples (6:17). These, not the city crowd, praise him; the Pharisees ask him to silence his disciples (19:39).

decisions.choice: peace; glory (every level)
decisions.reason: Key terms keep the same words at every level.

decisions.choice: There is peace in heaven; glory to God in the highest heaven
alternatives: Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest
decisions.reason: Readable makes a sentence of the first cry and names God as the one given glory, as in 2:14 (m3).

decisions.choice: the Lord
decisions.reason: As at John 1:23: in the New Testament the Greek word "Lord" is rendered "Lord"; meaning decision m1 notes that the Hebrew of Psalm 118 has the divine name.

decisions.choice: mighty deeds (B); miracles (R)
decisions.reason: As in 10:13.

decisions.choice: obras poderosas (L, B); milagros (R)
decisions.reason: The term used through the Gospels for these works of power (meaning decision m4); Readable says "milagros", as the English Readable says "miracles".

decisions.choice: dans les lieux très hauts (L); au plus haut des cieux (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "in the highest [places]", meaning heaven (m3). Literal keeps the plural place-word, as in Mark 11:10; Balanced and Readable say plainly that it is the highest heaven.

decisions.choice: matendo ya nguvu (L, B); miujiza (R)
decisions.reason: The term used through the Gospels for these works of power (meaning decision m4); Readable says "miujiza", as the English Readable says "miracles".

source.text: καί τινες τῶν Φαρισαίων ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν· Διδάσκαλε, ἐπιτίμησον τοῖς μαθηταῖς σου.

records.literal_gloss: And some of the Pharisees from the crowd said to him, Teacher, rebuke the disciples of you.

en.L: And some of the Pharisees from the crowd said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, rebuke {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples!"
en.B: Some Pharisees in the crowd said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, tell {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples to stop!"
en.R: Some of the Pharisees in the crowd said to Jesus, "Teacher, make {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} followers be quiet!"

es.L: Y algunos de los fariseos de entre la multitud {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «Maestro, reprende a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos».
es.B: Algunos fariseos que estaban entre la multitud {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «Maestro, ¡di a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos que paren!».
es.R: Algunos de los fariseos que estaban entre la gente le dijeron a Jesús: «Maestro, ¡haz que {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos se callen!».

fr.L: Et quelques-uns des Pharisiens, du milieu de la foule, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent : « Maître, réprimande {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples ! »
fr.B: Quelques Pharisiens qui étaient dans la foule {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent : « Maître, dis à {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples de se taire ! »
fr.R: Quelques Pharisiens qui étaient dans la foule ont dit à Jésus : « Maître, oblige {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples à se taire ! »

sw.L: Na baadhi ya Mafarisayo kutoka katika umati wakamwambia, "Mwalimu, wakemee wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}!"
sw.B: Baadhi ya Mafarisayo waliokuwa katika umati walimwambia, "Mwalimu, waambie wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} waache!"
sw.R: Baadhi ya Mafarisayo waliokuwa katika umati walimwambia Yesu, "Mwalimu, wanyamazishe wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}!"

decisions.choice: Pharisees: a Jewish movement devoted to keeping God's law in every part of life
decisions.reason: As explained at 5:17. This is the last time Luke's Gospel mentions them. They object to the disciples hailing Jesus as king, perhaps fearing the Roman governor's response, or because they reject the claim.

decisions.choice: rebuke: order to stop, correct sternly
decisions.reason: The word is used for a sharp command to stop (9:21, 42; 18:15, 39).

decisions.choice: Teacher: a respectful title, but no more
decisions.reason: The Pharisees call him teacher while the disciples call him king (7:40).

decisions.choice: tell your disciples to stop (B); make your followers be quiet (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the rebuke would do (m2).

decisions.choice: Maître
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:14: "Maître" is how French addresses a respected teacher; "Enseignant" and "Professeur" are job titles and sound like school.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Λέγω ὑμῖν, ὅτι ἐὰν οὗτοι σιωπήσουσιν, οἱ λίθοι κράξουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And answering he said, I say to you, that if these will be silent, the stones will cry out.

en.L: And answering, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I tell you that if these keep silent, the stones will cry out."
en.B: He answered, "I tell you, if these people were silent, the very stones would shout."
en.R: Jesus answered, "I tell you, if my followers stopped praising, the stones themselves would start shouting!"

es.L: Y respondiendo, dijo: «{{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que si estos callan, las piedras gritarán».
es.B: Él respondió: «{{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que, si estos se callaran, gritarían las mismas piedras».
es.R: Jesús respondió: «{{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que, si los discípulos dejaran de alabar, ¡las piedras mismas se pondrían a gritar!».

fr.L: Et, répondant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Je vous dis que, si ceux-ci se taisent, les pierres crieront. »
fr.B: Il répondit : « Je vous le dis : si eux se taisaient, ce sont les pierres qui crieraient. »
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Je vous le dis : si mes disciples arrêtaient de louer Dieu, les pierres elles-mêmes se mettraient à crier ! »

sw.L: Naye akajibu akasema, "Nawaambia kwamba hawa wakinyamaza, mawe yatapiga kelele."
sw.B: Akajibu, "Nawaambia, kama watu hawa wangenyamaza, mawe yenyewe yangepiga kelele."
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Nawaambia, kama wanafunzi wangeacha kusifu, mawe yenyewe yangeanza kupiga kelele!"

decisions.choice: the stones will cry out: the praise cannot be stopped; creation itself would give it
alternatives: the stones will cry out against Jerusalem in judgment
decisions.reason: The saying is a vivid way of saying that this moment must be greeted with praise. Habakkuk 2:11 speaks of a stone crying out from the wall against wrongdoing, which some hear here as a hint of judgment, and stones appear again in 19:44.

decisions.choice: if these will be silent: the future tense after "if" pictures a real possibility
alternatives: if these were to be silent
decisions.reason: The construction is unusual. The sense is the same: should the disciples be silent.

decisions.choice: that: introduces what Jesus says
decisions.reason: The word marks the start of the statement after "I tell you".

decisions.choice: would shout (B); would start shouting (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the case as a supposition, which fits the sense (m2).

decisions.choice: my followers stopped praising
decisions.reason: Readable says who "these" are and what they would stop doing.

source.text: Καὶ ὡς ἤγγισεν, ἰδὼν τὴν πόλιν ἔκλαυσεν ἐπ’ αὐτήν, λέγων ὅτι Εἰ ἔγνως ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ταύτῃ καὶ σὺ τὰ πρὸς εἰρήνην νῦν δὲ ἐκρύβη ἀπὸ ὀφθαλμῶν σου.

records.literal_gloss: And as he drew near, having seen the city he wept over it, \v 42 saying that If you had known in the day this even you the [things] for peace; but now it was hidden from eyes of you.

en.L: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} drew near, seeing the city, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wept over it, \v 42 saying, "If you, even you, had known on this day the things that make for peace! But now they have been hidden from your eyes.
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came nearer and saw the city, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wept over it. \v 42 "If only you too had known on this day the things that lead to peace!" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "But now they are hidden from your sight.
en.R: As Jesus came closer to Jerusalem, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw the city, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cried over it. \v 42 He said, "Jerusalem, I wish that today you had understood what would bring you peace! But now it is hidden from you, and you cannot see it.

es.L: Y cuando se acercó, al ver la ciudad, lloró por ella, \v 42 diciendo: «¡Si tú, aun tú, hubieras conocido en este día lo que conduce a la paz! Pero ahora ha quedado oculto a tus ojos.
es.B: Cuando se acercó más y vio la ciudad, lloró por ella. \v 42 «¡Si también tú hubieras reconocido en este día lo que lleva a la paz! —dijo—. Pero ahora está oculto a tus ojos.
es.R: Cuando Jesús se acercó más a Jerusalén, vio la ciudad y lloró por ella. \v 42 Dijo: «Jerusalén, ¡cómo quisiera que hoy hubieras entendido lo que te traería la paz! Pero ahora eso está escondido de ti, y no lo puedes ver.

fr.L: Et comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} approchait, voyant la ville, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pleura sur elle, \v 42 disant : « Si toi aussi tu avais connu, en ce jour, les choses [qui mènent] à la paix ! Mais maintenant elles ont été cachées à tes yeux.
fr.B: Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut plus près et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vit la ville, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pleura sur elle. \v 42 « Si seulement toi aussi tu avais reconnu en ce jour ce qui conduit à la paix ! dit-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}. Mais maintenant, cela est caché à tes yeux.
fr.R: Quand Jésus s’est approché de Jérusalem, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a vu la ville et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a pleuré sur elle. \v 42 Il a dit : « Jérusalem, si seulement tu avais compris aujourd’hui ce qui t’apporterait la paix ! Mais maintenant, c’est caché pour toi, et tu ne peux pas le voir.

sw.L: Na alipokaribia, akiuona mji, aliulilia, \v 42 akisema, "Laiti ungalijua katika siku hii, hata wewe, mambo ya amani! Lakini sasa yamefichwa machoni pako.
sw.B: Alipokaribia zaidi na kuuona mji, aliulilia. \v 42 Akasema, "Laiti wewe nawe ungalitambua katika siku hii mambo yaletayo amani! Lakini sasa yamefichwa usiyaone.
sw.R: Yesu alipokaribia Yerusalemu, aliuona mji, akaulilia. \v 42 Akasema, "Ee Yerusalemu, natamani leo ungekuwa umeelewa kile ambacho kingekuletea amani! Lakini sasa kimefichwa kwako, nawe huwezi kukiona.

decisions.choice: if you had known ...: a wish left unfinished, an expression of grief
alternatives: a condition with its result left out, "it would have saved you"
decisions.reason: The sentence begins as a condition and breaks off. It works as a cry of sorrow: if only you had known.

decisions.choice: the things for peace: what would bring peace with God and safety
alternatives: only a peace treaty with Rome
decisions.reason: The disciples have just sung of peace in heaven (19:38). Jerusalem's name was linked with peace (Hebrews 7:2; Psalm 122:6-8), but the city does not recognize the one who brings it. The war of 19:43-44 shows what follows.

decisions.choice: it was hidden: the way to peace is now hidden from the city
decisions.reason: The passive does not say who hid it. In Scripture God sometimes hides what people refuse to see (Isaiah 6:9-10; Luke 8:10; 18:34).

decisions.choice: wept: cried aloud
decisions.reason: The verb is used of loud weeping (6:21; 7:13; 8:52). Jesus grieves over the city that will reject him.

decisions.choice: on this day: the day the king comes to the city
decisions.reason: "This day" is the day of Jesus' coming; 19:44 calls it the time of the city's visitation.

decisions.choice: peace (every level)
decisions.reason: A key term (m2).

decisions.choice: Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable names the city Jesus speaks to.

decisions.choice: Jesus' words open here and close at the end of 19:44
decisions.reason: The next sentence continues his words.

decisions.choice: Laiti ungalijua / ungalitambua
decisions.reason: The Greek "if" clause is a wish left unfinished, an expression of grief (meaning decision m1). "Laiti" is the Swahili word for such a wish (if only), so the sentence can stand without a second half; "kama" would leave the reader waiting for one.

source.text: ὅτι ἥξουσιν ἡμέραι ἐπὶ σὲ καὶ παρεμβαλοῦσιν οἱ ἐχθροί σου χάρακά σοι καὶ περικυκλώσουσίν σε καὶ συνέξουσίν σε πάντοθεν, καὶ ἐδαφιοῦσίν σε καὶ τὰ τέκνα σου ἐν σοί, καὶ οὐκ ἀφήσουσιν λίθον ἐπὶ λίθον ἐν σοί, ἀνθ’ ὧν οὐκ ἔγνως τὸν καιρὸν τῆς ἐπισκοπῆς σου.

records.literal_gloss: because will come days upon you and will throw up the enemies of you a palisade against you and will surround you and will hem in you from every side, \v 44 and will dash to the ground you and the children of you in you, and not will they leave stone upon stone in you, because not you knew the time of the visitation of you.

en.L: For days will come upon you when your enemies will set up a palisade against you and surround you and hem you in on every side, \v 44 and they will dash you to the ground, and your children within you, and they will not leave stone upon stone in you, because you did not know the time of your visitation."
en.B: For a time is coming for you when your enemies will build a siege wall against you. They will encircle you and press in on you from all sides. \v 44 They will level you to the ground, you and your children inside you. They will leave no stone on top of another within you, because you did not recognize the time when God came to visit you."
en.R: The time is coming when your enemies will build a wall around you. They will surround you and close in on you from every side. \v 44 They will destroy you completely, and they will kill the people who live inside your walls. They will not leave even one stone on top of another. This will happen because you did not understand that God had come to save you."

es.L: Porque vendrán días sobre ti en que tus enemigos levantarán contra ti una empalizada, y te rodearán, y te estrecharán por todas partes, \v 44 y te arrasarán hasta el suelo, a ti y a tus hijos dentro de ti, y no dejarán en ti piedra sobre piedra, porque no conociste el tiempo de tu visitación».
es.B: Porque vendrá un tiempo en que tus enemigos levantarán contra ti un cerco de asedio. Te rodearán y te apretarán por todos lados. \v 44 Te derribarán hasta el suelo, a ti y a tus hijos dentro de ti. No dejarán dentro de ti ni una piedra sobre otra, porque no reconociste el tiempo en que Dios vino a visitarte».
es.R: Llegará el día en que tus enemigos construirán un muro a tu alrededor. Te rodearán y te encerrarán por todos lados. \v 44 Te destruirán por completo y matarán a la gente que vive dentro de tus murallas. No dejarán ni una piedra encima de otra. Esto sucederá porque no entendiste que Dios había venido a salvarte».

fr.L: Car des jours viendront sur toi où tes ennemis élèveront contre toi une palissade, t’encercleront et te serreront de tous côtés ; \v 44 ils te jetteront à terre, toi et tes enfants au milieu de toi, et ils ne laisseront pas en toi pierre sur pierre, parce que tu n’as pas reconnu le temps de ta visitation. »
fr.B: Car un temps va venir pour toi où tes ennemis construiront contre toi un mur de siège. Ils t’encercleront et te presseront de tous côtés. \v 44 Ils te jetteront à terre, toi et tes enfants qui vivent dans tes murs. Ils ne laisseront pas chez toi une pierre sur une autre, parce que tu n’as pas reconnu le moment où Dieu est venu te visiter. »
fr.R: Le moment arrive où tes ennemis construiront un mur tout autour de toi. Ils t’encercleront et t’enfermeront de tous les côtés. \v 44 Ils te détruiront complètement, et ils tueront les gens qui vivent à l’intérieur de tes murs. Ils ne laisseront même pas une pierre sur une autre. Cela va arriver parce que tu n’as pas compris que Dieu était venu pour te sauver. »

sw.L: Kwa maana siku zitakujia ambapo adui zako watakujengea boma, na kukuzunguka, na kukubana pande zote, \v 44 nao watakuangusha chini, wewe na watoto wako walio ndani yako, wala hawataacha ndani yako jiwe juu ya jiwe, kwa sababu hukujua wakati wa kujiliwa kwako."
sw.B: Kwa maana wakati unakuja ambapo adui zako watajenga ukuta wa kukuzingira. Watakuzunguka na kukubana kila upande. \v 44 Watakusawazisha na ardhi, wewe na watoto wako walio ndani yako. Hawataacha jiwe juu ya jiwe jingine ndani yako, kwa sababu hukutambua wakati ambapo Mungu alikuja kukutembelea."
sw.R: Wakati unakuja ambapo adui zako watajenga ukuta kukuzunguka. Watakuzingira na kukubana kutoka kila upande. \v 44 Watakuangamiza kabisa, na kuwaua watu wanaoishi ndani ya kuta zako. Hawataacha hata jiwe moja juu ya jingine. Haya yatatokea kwa sababu hukuelewa kwamba Mungu alikuwa amekuja kukuokoa."

decisions.choice: palisade: a siege wall of stakes and earth built around a city
decisions.reason: Besiegers built such walls to cut a city off. In AD 70 the Roman army under Titus surrounded Jerusalem with a siege wall, took the city and destroyed the temple.

decisions.choice: dash you to the ground, and your children: the language of the prophets for a city's fall
decisions.reason: The words recall Isaiah 29:3 (the LORD will besiege Jerusalem with siegeworks), Psalm 137:9 and Hosea 10:14 (children dashed down). "Your children" means the city's people.

decisions.choice: the time of your visitation: the time when God came to you
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament God "visits" his people to help or to judge them. Zechariah praised God for visiting his people to redeem them (1:68, 78), and the crowd at Nain said God had visited his people (7:16). Jerusalem did not see that God had come to it in Jesus.

decisions.choice: not leave stone upon stone: destroy completely
alternatives: only the temple will be destroyed
decisions.reason: The city will be so ruined that its buildings fall stone from stone. Jesus says the same of the temple in 21:6.

decisions.choice: the time when God came to visit you (B); that God had come to save you (R)
decisions.reason: "Visitation" is no longer used in this sense. Balanced says who came; Readable says why he came, as in 1:68 and 7:16 (m3). Literal keeps "visitation".

decisions.choice: destroy you completely; kill the people who live inside your walls
alternatives: dash to the ground you and your children
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m2).

decisions.choice: una empalizada (L); un cerco de asedio (B); un muro (R)
decisions.reason: A palisade of stakes and earth built round a city under siege (meaning decision m1). Literal names the thing; Balanced says what it was for; Readable says "muro", as the English Readable says "wall".

decisions.choice: le temps de ta visitation (L); le moment où Dieu est venu te visiter (B); que Dieu était venu pour te sauver (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps "visitation", the word French Bibles have used for God coming to his people, though most readers now know it as the name of a Marian feast; "visite" would sound like a social call. Balanced says who came, and Readable why (m3).

decisions.choice: boma (L); ukuta wa kukuzingira (B); ukuta (R)
decisions.reason: A palisade of stakes and earth built round a city under siege (meaning decision m1). "Boma" is a fence or stockade of stakes; Balanced says what it was for, and Readable says "ukuta", as the English Readable says "wall". "Ngome" is a fortress, the city's own defence.

source.text: Καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἤρξατο ἐκβάλλειν τοὺς πωλοῦντας, λέγων αὐτοῖς· Γέγραπται· Καὶ ἔσται ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς, ὑμεῖς δὲ αὐτὸν ἐποιήσατε σπήλαιον λῃστῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And having entered into the temple he began to drive out the [ones] selling, \v 46 saying to them, It has been written, And will be the house of me a house of prayer, but you it made a cave of robbers.

en.L: And entering the temple, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to drive out those who were selling, \v 46 saying to them, "It is written, 'And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house shall be a house of prayer,' but you have made it a cave of robbers."
en.B: Then Jesus went into the temple and began to throw out the people who were selling there. \v 46 He said to them, "Scripture says, 'My house will be a house of prayer.' But you have turned it into a hideout for robbers."
en.R: Jesus went into the temple courts and began to force out the people who were selling things there. \v 46 He said to them, "The Scriptures say, 'My house will be a place where people pray.' But you have made it a hiding place for robbers!"

es.L: Y entrando en el templo, comenzó a echar fuera a los que vendían, \v 46 diciéndoles: «Está escrito: “Y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} casa será casa de oración”, pero {{plural_you:ustedes la han hecho|vosotros la habéis hecho}} cueva de bandidos».
es.B: Luego Jesús entró en el templo y comenzó a echar fuera a los que vendían allí. \v 46 Les dijo: «La Escritura dice: “Mi casa será casa de oración”. Pero {{plural_you:ustedes la han convertido|vosotros la habéis convertido}} en guarida de bandidos».
es.R: Jesús entró en los patios del templo y comenzó a sacar a la gente que estaba vendiendo cosas allí. \v 46 Les dijo: «La Escritura dice: “Mi casa será un lugar donde la gente ore”. ¡Pero {{plural_you:ustedes la han convertido|vosotros la habéis convertido}} en un escondite de bandidos!».

fr.L: Et, étant entré dans le temple, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se mit à chasser ceux qui vendaient, \v 46 leur disant : « Il est écrit : “Et {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} maison sera une maison de prière”, mais vous, vous en avez fait une caverne de brigands. »
fr.B: Puis Jésus entra dans la cour du temple et se mit à chasser ceux qui y vendaient. \v 46 Il leur dit : « L’Écriture dit : “Ma maison sera une maison de prière.” Mais vous, vous en avez fait un repaire de bandits. »
fr.R: Jésus est entré dans la cour du temple. Il a commencé à mettre dehors les gens qui vendaient des choses à cet endroit. \v 46 Il leur a dit : « Les Écritures disent : “Ma maison sera un endroit où les gens prient.” Mais vous, vous en avez fait une cachette pour les voleurs ! »

sw.L: Na akiisha kuingia hekaluni, alianza kuwafukuza nje wale waliokuwa wakiuza, \v 46 akiwaambia, "Imeandikwa, 'Na nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itakuwa nyumba ya maombi,' lakini ninyi mmeifanya pango la wanyang'anyi."
sw.B: Kisha Yesu aliingia hekaluni, akaanza kuwafukuza watu waliokuwa wakiuza humo. \v 46 Akawaambia, "Maandiko yanasema, 'Nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itakuwa nyumba ya maombi.' Lakini ninyi mmeigeuza kuwa maficho ya wanyang'anyi."
sw.R: Yesu aliingia katika nyua za hekalu, akaanza kuwafukuza watu waliokuwa wakiuza vitu humo. \v 46 Akawaambia, "Maandiko yanasema, 'Nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itakuwa mahali ambapo watu wanaomba.' Lakini ninyi mmeigeuza kuwa mahali pa kujificha wanyang'anyi!"

decisions.choice: the temple: the whole temple area with its outer courts, where animals for sacrifice were sold
decisions.reason: The word means the temple with its courts. Traders sold animals and birds for the sacrifices and changed money for the temple tax in the outer court.

decisions.choice: my house shall be a house of prayer: Isaiah 56:7
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 56:7 God promises that foreigners who hold fast to his covenant will be brought to his holy mountain, for his house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples. "My" is God speaking. Luke quotes the first part only.

decisions.choice: a cave of robbers: Jeremiah 7:11
decisions.reason: Jeremiah stood at the temple gate and asked whether the house called by God's name had become a robbers' cave in the people's eyes, because they sinned and then came to the temple as if it made them safe (Jeremiah 7:1-15). Robbers hide in caves between their raids. Jeremiah went on to warn that the temple would be destroyed.

decisions.choice: those who were selling: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: those who were selling in it and those who were buying, as in many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "in it, and those who were buying", which matches Mark 11:15. The shorter text has early support. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: robbers: bandits who take by force
decisions.reason: The word means a bandit or armed robber, as in 10:30.

decisions.choice: a cave of robbers (L); a hideout for robbers (B); a hiding place for robbers (R)
decisions.reason: "Den" is now used mostly of an animal's lair, and "thieves" is weaker than the word. The renderings say what a robbers' cave was for (m3).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} (L); My, capitalized either way at the start of the quotation (B, R)
decisions.reason: God is the speaker in Isaiah 56:7.

decisions.choice: a place where people pray
decisions.reason: Readable says what the phrase means.

decisions.choice: temple courts
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the selling was in the courts (m1).

decisions.choice: bandidos
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a robber who uses violence, a bandit (meaning decision m5), not a sneak thief; "ladrones" usually means thieves. As in Matthew 21:13.

decisions.choice: Está escrito (L); La Escritura dice (B, R)
decisions.reason: The formula used through the Gospels, following the English "It is written" (L) and "Scripture says" (B, R).

decisions.choice: le temple (L); la cour du temple (B, R) (for the whole chapter)
alternatives: le temple at every level, as the English Balanced
decisions.reason: As the style guide settles for this word and as Luke 2 and Mark 11 have it: the selling and the teaching took place in the open courts, not in the sanctuary (m1). The English Balanced keeps "temple"; French Balanced follows the term sheet, as the English Readable says "temple courts".

decisions.choice: une caverne de brigands (L); un repaire de bandits (B); une cachette pour les voleurs (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 11:17: the word means bandits who take by force (m5), stronger than "voleurs"; Readable uses the common word and says what the cave was for.

decisions.choice: Nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, with a span at every level
alternatives: yangu with no span, as the English Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The English "My" opens the quotation in Balanced and Readable and is capitalised anyway, so it has no span there (decision r-en-2). Swahili puts the possessive after the noun, where it can take the setting, as in Matthew 21:13.

decisions.choice: wanyang'anyi
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a robber who uses violence, a bandit (meaning decision m5), not a thief ("mwizi"). "Wanyang'anyi" is the term the shared term sheet sets for this word, as in John 18:40.

source.text: Καὶ ἦν διδάσκων τὸ καθ’ ἡμέραν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ· οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν ἀπολέσαι καὶ οἱ πρῶτοι τοῦ λαοῦ, καὶ οὐχ εὕρισκον τὸ τί ποιήσωσιν, ὁ λαὸς γὰρ ἅπας ἐξεκρέματο αὐτοῦ ἀκούων.

records.literal_gloss: And he was teaching day by day in the temple; but the chief priests and the scribes were seeking him to destroy and the leading [men] of the people, \v 48 and not they were finding what they might do, the people for all were hanging on him listening.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes were seeking to destroy {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and [so were] the leading men of the people, \v 48 and they did not find what they might do, for all the people were hanging on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, listening.
en.B: Every day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught in the temple. The chief priests and the scribes wanted to kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and so did the leaders of the people. \v 48 But they could find no way to do it, because all the people clung to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, listening to every word.
en.R: Every day Jesus taught in the temple courts. The chief priests and the teachers of the law wanted to kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. The other leaders of the people wanted this too. \v 48 But they could not find a way to do it, because all the people were listening closely to everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said.

es.L: Y enseñaba cada día en el templo. Pero los jefes de los sacerdotes y los escribas procuraban acabar con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y [también] los principales del pueblo; \v 48 y no hallaban qué hacer, porque todo el pueblo estaba pendiente de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, escuchándolo.
es.B: Todos los días enseñaba en el templo. Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los escribas querían matarlo, y también los dirigentes del pueblo. \v 48 Pero no encontraban la manera de hacerlo, porque todo el pueblo estaba pendiente de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, sin perder palabra.
es.R: Jesús enseñaba todos los días en los patios del templo. Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los maestros de la ley querían matarlo. Los otros líderes del pueblo querían lo mismo. \v 48 Pero no encontraban la manera de hacerlo, porque toda la gente escuchaba con mucha atención todo lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} decía.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} enseignait chaque jour dans le temple. Mais les chefs des prêtres et les scribes cherchaient à {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire périr, et [aussi] les premiers du peuple ; \v 48 et ils ne trouvaient pas ce qu’ils pourraient faire, car tout le peuple, en {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}écoutant, était suspendu à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} lèvres.
fr.B: Chaque jour, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} enseignait dans la cour du temple. Les chefs des prêtres et les scribes voulaient {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire mourir, et les notables du peuple aussi. \v 48 Mais ils ne trouvaient pas comment s’y prendre, car le peuple tout entier était suspendu à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} lèvres.
fr.R: Chaque jour, Jésus enseignait dans la cour du temple. Les chefs des prêtres et les spécialistes de la Loi voulaient {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tuer. Les autres chefs du peuple le voulaient aussi. \v 48 Mais ils ne trouvaient pas le moyen de le faire, parce que tout le peuple écoutait avec attention tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} disait.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akifundisha kila siku hekaluni. Lakini wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi walikuwa wakitafuta kumwangamiza, na [vivyo hivyo] wakuu wa watu, \v 48 wala hawakuona la kufanya, kwa maana watu wote walikuwa wakimng'ang'ania, wakimsikiliza.
sw.B: Kila siku alikuwa akifundisha hekaluni. Wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi walitaka kumwua, na viongozi wa watu vilevile. \v 48 Lakini hawakupata njia ya kufanya hivyo, kwa sababu watu wote walishikamana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, wakisikiliza kila neno.
sw.R: Kila siku Yesu alifundisha katika nyua za hekalu. Wakuu wa makuhani na walimu wa sheria walitaka kumwua. Viongozi wengine wa watu nao walitaka hivyo. \v 48 Lakini hawakupata njia ya kufanya hivyo, kwa sababu watu wote walikuwa wakisikiliza kwa makini kila kitu alichosema.

decisions.choice: the chief priests, the scribes, the leading men of the people: the groups that made up the ruling council
decisions.reason: The senior priests, the experts in the law and the leading laymen of Jerusalem formed the council that would hand Jesus over (9:22; 22:66). Jesus had foretold that these men would reject him.

decisions.choice: were hanging on him, listening: listened eagerly, holding on to every word
decisions.reason: The verb pictures someone hanging from a support. The people held on to Jesus' words, and their support kept the leaders from acting openly.

decisions.choice: destroy: put to death
decisions.reason: The verb is used for killing (6:9; 17:27).

decisions.choice: was teaching day by day: his regular practice during these days
decisions.reason: Luke describes Jesus' daily teaching in the temple (21:37-38; 22:53).

decisions.choice: the chief priests and the teachers of the law (R); the chief priests and the scribes (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in 9:22: "scribes" today suggests people who copy documents, so Readable says what these men did.

decisions.choice: clung to him, listening to every word
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of holding on (m2) in plainer words.

decisions.choice: los jefes de los sacerdotes; los escribas (L, B), los maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: The terms used through the Gospels. Readable says what the scribes were, teachers of the law, as the English Readable does (decision r-en-1).

decisions.choice: les chefs des prêtres (every level); les scribes (L, B), les spécialistes de la Loi (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms, as in Mark 11:18. "Les grands prêtres" would blur the line with "le grand prêtre" himself; Readable follows the English "teachers of the law".

decisions.choice: était suspendu à ses lèvres (L, B)
decisions.reason: French has an idiom with the same picture as the Greek "hanging on him" (m2), "être suspendu aux lèvres de quelqu’un", so Literal and Balanced can keep the image; a word-for-word "suspendu à lui" would not be understood. Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: wakuu wa makuhani; waandishi (L, B), walimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: The terms used through the Gospels. Readable says what the scribes were, teachers of the law, as the English Readable does (decision r-en-1).
